name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (with the 1017 update)

lineage.how_derived: trained from scratch on 45T multimodal tokens, then SFT, RL and on-policy distillation (card). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (2026-10-17) is a minor update of the same architecture with better reasoning, coding, agent and visual scores and shorter outputs. No separate Base repository exists (the Base row in the card table is a benchmark column; the repo name DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Base does not resolve, 2026-11-19).

purpose: The card presents a multimodal MoE whose point is KV-cache compression (title: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression): a causal encoder-decoder activates only 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decode, with 4x smaller global KV cache than DeepSeek-V4-Flash, for 1M-token agentic work. The 1017 release targets faster, cheaper task completion across agent harnesses.

license.name: MIT
license.notes: LICENSE read in both repos (identical, 1084 bytes): standard MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 DeepSeek, to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense and/or sell. The card states the repository and the model weights are under it.

architecture.kind: multimodal sparse MoE with causal encoder-decoder (CED), compressed sparse attention 2 (CSA2), Single-Pass mHC, Engram memory tables and DSpark drafter
architecture.gguf_arch: deepseek_v41 (supported by llama.cpp since release b11870, 2026-10-25, per the ISTA-DASLab card)
architecture.attention: 20-layer causal encoder then 20-layer decoder; MQA with 1 KV head of dim 512, sliding window 128, top-512 hierarchical sparse indexer, each layer in Full, Reindex or Reuse mode
architecture.drafter: DSpark speculative decoding (semi-autoregressive draft, 3 MTP layers in config); standalone DSpark GGUFs of about 8 GB exist (unsloth, kyuz0)
architecture.why_this_design: The card says CED lets the decoder's global KV cache come from the encoder's final hidden states, so only 8B parameters are active in prefill and 16B in decode; CSA2 shares main KV and indexer keys across layers and reuses top-K indices, giving about 4x and 437x smaller KV cache than DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V1. 552B are the backbone, 196B (196.6B per ISTA) are Engram tables read sparsely per token, total 763B per the ISTA card.

strengths: Very high vendor agent and coding numbers (max effort) for a model that has quants fitting 128 GB of RAM
Tiny KV cache and 16B active parameters in decode
Quantises well with GSQ-RCO: IQ2_XXS matches the base on three benchmarks (quantisers' own run)
weaknesses: 552B backbone plus 196B Engram: the best fit is the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class only
All headline scores are vendor scores at maximum reasoning effort with 1M-token contexts; local runs will use less
Engram tables need a fast SSD
soft.behavior: Recommended sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 or 1.0, max_tokens at least 256K (card); reasoning effort is a continuous 1 to 100 setting, vendor results use 100, the ISTA quant evaluation used 50. No Jinja template in the release.
best_for: agentic coding and terminal work on the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class
avoid_for: machines under about 128 GB of RAM
soft.maturity: DeepSeek is an established lab; the V4.1 line has two releases in five weeks, a Pareto-update (1017) and a large quant ecosystem (about 100 derivatives on the HF API for each release).

tona_fit.reason: Best vendor agent and coding numbers combined with a verified MIT licence and quants that hold their quality at 1.75 to 2 bits (quantisers' own test); it fits only the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class (120.7 GB backbone). For the 24 GB and smaller classes only the pruned coder derivative (72 GB resident) comes close and still does not fit below 24 GB. Judged on quality, licence and hardware class; Tona has no module for it yet.
blockers: Tona has no DeepSeek-V4 module (MQA, indexer, hyper-connections, Engram): engine support, not quality
no independent agent evaluation of the quants beyond the quantisers' three benchmarks
does not fit the 16 GB + 64 GB reference class
